correctness.rationale: Constant barycentric weights on independent subgroup orbits identify the actual geometric fixed spaces with independence complexes of the compatibility graphs, not with invariants of homology. Folding the columns gives L_(n+1) for v. For hv the center is blocked when n is even (giving L_n); when n is odd it is an admissible apex on the last rung of G_floor(n/2). A terminal pair of leaves on adjacent supports permits an open-neighborhood fold deleting one support, then a cone collapse. The link of the odd-case apex is exactly such an even half-chain, so its cone collapses relative to the link. Chandrakar–Singh supplies the ordinary wedge for the remaining intact half-chain; the n=1 triangle gives three points separately. The independent even-column row-pairs give the h simplex, and reversing them gives the V4 simplex on ceil(n/2) orbits. Independently constructed orbit graphs and mod-2 reduced Betti numbers agreed in all 12 subgroup/size cases n=1,2,3. No frozen script was run; the finite check does not prove the theorem.
residual_risks: Finite ranks are mod two and restricted to n≤3; the homotopy conclusion rests on the explicit collapses and the cited ordinary homotopy theorem.

No materially distinct contribution in the frozen classification is established.

value.rationale: The geometric fixed diagram is a natural object, and geometrical types contain more information than characters alone. Here the established orbit-graph diagram already provides the actual spaces: the additions are the routine collapse of a terminal-leaf fold to a cone, the relative cone removal on that same link, and the fixed simplex under a reversal. No separate new structural invariant or nonroutine fixed-space distinction remains once this stronger concrete model information is credited.
residual_risks: The verdict does not devalue fixed-space classification problems generally and does not dispute the mathematical types in this example.
